extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how postsecondary institutions must handle access to, review of, and protection of evidence in Title IX sex-based harassment grievance procedures, including use of investigative reports, timing, privacy, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of evidence: 'relevant and not otherwise impermissible' (§106.2/§106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties must have access to evidence that is relevant to the allegations of sex-based harassment and not otherwise impermissible; the decisionmaker must evaluate that same scope of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department defines 'relevant' to limit recipient discretion; the scope of evidence the parties may access and what the decisionmaker may rely on are coextensive. Institutions must include both inculpatory and exculpatory evidence consistent with the definition of 'relevant' in §106.2 and §106.45(b)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on evidence about complainant's sexual predisposition or prior sexual behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are not permitted access to evidence relating to the complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct unless it falls within two narrow exceptions in §106.45(b)(7)(iii): (1) offered to prove someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct; or (2) concerns specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent and is offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This departs from the 2020 approach that allowed broader inspection; only evidence meeting one of the two exceptions is 'relevant' and permitted in investigative reports and hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access evidence (§106.46(e)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must provide each party and the party's advisor an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence either by providing access to the underlying evidence or by providing access to an investigative report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal opportunity means the parties must have the same opportunity to access the evidence (same universe of evidence and cannot give one party the evidence and another the report), but need not be identical in mode (e.g., auxiliary aids for disability or language assistance may differ). Institutions cannot provide different versions of an investigative report to different parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative report option: written investigative report requirement and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the institution provides access to an investigative report, it must be a written investigative report, and the report must accurately summarize the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions violate §106.46(e)(6)(i) by providing an investigative report that fails to accurately summarize relevant evidence; if any party requests access to the underlying evidence after receiving the report, the institution must provide access to the underlying evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence option: access to underlying evidence (modes and limitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution may provide parties access to the actual underlying evidence instead of an investigative report; §106.46(e)(6) does not require providing physical or electronic copies but does require an equal opportunity to access the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions have discretion on mode (electronic copies, physical copies, onsite inspection), need not attach documentary evidence to an investigative report, and must ensure accessibility for disabilities and limited English proficiency; they should consider resources and case complexity when choosing mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions must articulate consistent principles in grievance procedures (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must articulate consistent principles for determining whether and when the institution will initially provide access to the underlying evidence or an investigative report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles could consider roles of parties, nature of conduct alleged, severity of potential sanctions, volume/format of evidence, and institutional resources; institutions cannot decide ad hoc without written consistent principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable opportunity to review and respond to evidence (§106.46(e)(6)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties and their advisors must have a reasonable opportunity to review and respond to the evidence or the investigative report before the institution determines whether sex-based harassment occurred (and before any hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'reasonable' standard accommodates variation in evidence volume and complexity; institutions may set timeframes but must ensure parties can meaningfully review (e.g., hundreds of pages vs. short files). Institutions must allow reasonable extensions for good cause under §106.46(e)(5). Institutions may permit responses before, during, or after a hearing, and must allow others to review/respond to any post-hearing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to provide audio/audiovisual recording or transcript of questioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must provide the parties with an audio or audiovisual recording or transcript of the questioning of parties and witnesses as part of the process for assessing credibility (if individual meetings are held) and in live hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement applies regardless of whether the institution opts for the investigative report or evidence option; it helps parties assess credibility and prepare responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker reliance limited to evidence to which parties had access
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker cannot rely on evidence in reaching a determination if the parties were not given access to that evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §106.46(h)(1)(iii), the written determination must include the decisionmaker's evaluation of the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence — the same evidence to which parties were given equal opportunity to access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against unauthorized disclosures (§106.46(e)(6)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions must take reasonable steps to prevent parties and advisors from unauthorized disclosure of evidence and information obtained solely through the sex-based harassment grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable steps may include policies, technical protections (software limits), and informing parties which disclosures are permissible (e.g., disclosures authorized under §106.45(b)(5) such as to family or confidential resources). Institutions may penalize unauthorized disclosures but are not required to prescribe a particular penalty; they must implement this consistent with the First Amendment and §106.6(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interplay with §106.45(b)(5) privacy protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on disclosure in §106.46(e)(6)(iii) are narrowly framed to address information obtained solely through grievance procedures and operate alongside §106.45(b)(5)'s broader requirement to take reasonable steps to protect parties' and witnesses' privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized disclosures include those permitted under §106.45(b)(5); institutions must ensure privacy protections do not unreasonably restrict a party's ability to consult family/confidential advisors or prepare participation in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to provide draft investigative reports for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions are not required to provide parties the opportunity to respond to or comment upon draft investigative reports, because that could unnecessarily prolong proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties retain the opportunity to review and respond to the investigative report under §106.46(e)(6)(ii) and to provide input during the investigation via witnesses and evidence under §106.45(f)(2). Institutions may allow further submissions post-hearing if warranted, but must ensure opposing parties can review/respond to any new evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions' discretion on manner of providing access (subject to equal opportunity and reasonable review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond requiring an equal opportunity to access relevant evidence and a reasonable opportunity to review, the regulations do not prescribe a particular manner for sharing evidence or attaching documents to investigative reports; institutions have discretion but must exercise it to ensure equality and meaningful review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretion should account for case complexity, evidence volume, institutional resources, accessibility needs, and the possibility of later requests for underlying evidence if an investigative report was provided initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing parties of their rights to access evidence and investigative report
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must inform parties that they are entitled to an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an investigative report and, if an investigative report is provided, that they are entitled to access the underlying evidence upon request of any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text (§106.46(c)(2)(iii)) specifically requires notice to parties; this helps prevent unequal access and ensures parties know how to request underlying materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and conflict-of-interest rules for investigators and decisionmakers (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as an investigator or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias; bias is a ground for appeal under §106.46(i)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must screen investigators/decisionmakers for conflicts and bias and must abide by appeal remedies when conflicts/bias that would change outcome are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and enforcement remedies for failure to comply with evidence-access requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may appeal determinations on bases including procedural irregularity that would change the outcome, new evidence not reasonably available before determination, and conflict/bias; OCR can investigate recipient noncompliance with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on circumstances, an institution's failure to comply with §106.46(e)(6) may be the basis for an appeal under §106.46(i) or for OCR enforcement action (see OCR Enforcement discussion).
